'''Burudi Ali Johnson'''<ref name="BBCObit">{{cite web |last=McKenna |first=Lorraine |date=2025-09-23 |title=Rudi Johnson: Former Cincinnati Bengals running back dies aged 45 |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/american-football/articles/cp987d0xn4eo |access-date=2025-10-02 |website=BBC Sport}}</ref> (October 1, 1979 – September 23, 2025) was an American professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for eight seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), primarily with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]] and was selected by the Bengals in the fourth round of the [[2001 NFL draft]].

Johnson was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] with the Bengals in [[2005 Pro Bowl|2004]] after leading the team in rushing. He employed a bruising style of hard-nosed running that earned him the nickname the "Auburn Rambler."

'''Ruben Parnell Brown''' (born February 13, 1972) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Guard (American football)|guard]] for 13 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh Panthers]]. He was selected by the [[Buffalo Bills]] 14th overall in the [[1995 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1995 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1995/draft.htm |access-date=2023-03-31|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Brown played nine seasons for the Bills and four more for the [[Chicago Bears]], starting all 181 games in which he played. He was a four-time [[All-Pro]] and nine-time [[Pro Bowl]] selection, including eight consecutive Pro Bowl selections with the Bills from 1996 to 2003. He is the older brother of former NFL linebacker [[Cornell Brown]].

Brown attended [[E. C. Glass High School]] in [[Lynchburg, Virginia]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.pittsburghpanthers.com/blog/2012/08/ruben-browns-pitt-path-to-nfl-stardom.html|title = Story Archives | work=UPMC LiveWire - The Official Athletic Blog of the University of Pittsburgh }}</ref>

'''Roy Lee Williams''' (born August 14, 1980), is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) for nine seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors.  He was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] eighth overall in the [[2002 NFL draft]], where he earned five straight [[Pro Bowl]] selections from 2003 to 2007. He spent the last two years of his career with the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], before retiring in 2011.

Williams was considered by some to be one of the most violent hitters in football during his playing career, and sometimes received criticism for his perceived “dirty” play-style.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/64952-the-dirtiest-player-in-all-of-sports/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210803022330/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/64952-the-dirtiest-player-in-all-of-sports|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 3, 2021|title=The Dirtiest Player in All Of Sports|website=[[Bleacher Report]] }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportscroll.com/26-dirtiest-nfl-players-of-all-time/20/|title=26 Dirtiest NFL Players Of All-Time|date=July 11, 2019 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2011/08/24/safety-roy-williams-turns-down-contract-offer-takes-media-job/|title=Safety Roy Williams turns down contract offer, takes media job|date=August 24, 2011 }}</ref><ref name="chron.com">[http://www.chron.com/disp/story.mpl/sports/fb/texansfront/5392642.html Cowboys' Williams loses appeal with NFL | Chron.com - Houston Chronicle]</ref>
Williams is currently a sideline reporter for Oklahoma football games.

'''Rudolph Barber''' (born December 24, 1943) is a former collegiate and professional [[American football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Bethune-Cookman University|Bethune-Cookman]], and played professionally in the [[American Football League]] for the [[Miami Dolphins]] in [[1968 AFL season|1968]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rudy Barber|publisher=Pro Football Reference|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BarbRu20.htm|accessdate=2010-08-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Archdeacon|first=Tom|title=Rudy Barber still feels racism caused his release|work=The Miami News|date=1977-08-02|url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ADs0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=o-sFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3221,926788|accessdate=2010-08-29|archive-date=2020-03-28|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200328063315/https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=ADs0AAAAIBAJ&sjid=o-sFAAAAIBAJ&pg=3221,926788|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He currently [[pastor]]s a church in [[Carol City, Florida]], and serves as the [[chaplain]] to the neighboring Miami Carol City Chiefs Football team. It is the same school which he coached at for several years and sent three of his children—Rudy Barber Jr, [[Kantroy Barber]], and Misti Barber—who all went on to win All Dade honors and athlete of the year, and compete on the [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] college level. Rudy Jr, played on the [[University of Miami]] national championship teams in 1989 and 1991, and Kantroy played with the [[New England Patriots]] during their [[Super Bowl]] run which ended with a loss to the eventual champions [[Green Bay Packers]] in [[New Orleans]]. Misti was formerly a member of the [[University of Miami]] [[track and field]] team. Recently Barber's grandson Quynn attended Carol City becoming a two sport star playing every offensive down his senior year, and gaining All Dade Honors and a state qualifier in the [[shot put]] on his track team.

'''Carl Roy Gerela''' (born April 2, 1948) is a Canadian former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[placekicker]] in the [[American Football League]] (AFL) and [[National Football League]] (NFL). He won three [[Super Bowl]]s with the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].

Gerela graduated from [[Kalani High School]] in [[Honolulu]], and played [[college football]] for the [[New Mexico State Aggies football|New Mexico State Aggies]].  He was selected in the [[1969 NFL/AFL draft#Round four|fourth round]] of the [[1969 NFL/AFL draft]] by the [[1969 Houston Oilers season|Houston Oilers]] and played for them in the [[American Football League]] in [[1969 Houston Oilers season|1969]], as well as their first NFL season of [[1970 Houston Oilers season|1970]].

Gerela signed with the Steelers before the [[1971 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1971]] season, and quickly became popular with Steelers fans, inspiring a fan club, "Gerela's Gorillas." He led the [[American Football Conference|AFC]] in scoring in [[1973 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1973]] and [[1974 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1974]], and was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] in [[1972 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1972]] and 1974. When he retired, he had the record for most missed extra points in postseason history (6) until [[Jake Elliott]] matched him in 2026.<ref>https://x.com/JoshDubowAP/status/2010472387855503795?t=e6BaRLclUk8mtaXtU6Y1qA&s=19</ref>

Gerela was a member of the Steelers' Super Bowl championship teams in 1974, [[1975 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1975]], and [[1978 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1978]], but was released before the [[1979 Pittsburgh Steelers season|1979]] season in favor of rookie [[Matt Bahr]]. He appeared in three games for the [[1979 San Diego Chargers season|San Diego Chargers]] in 1979 before a torn groin muscle ended his career.

Gerela ranks fourth on the Steelers' all-time scoring list, behind [[Gary Anderson (placekicker)|Gary Anderson]], [[Jeff Reed (American football)|Jeff Reed]], and [[Chris Boswell]].<ref>{{cite news |first= Ed|last= Bouchette|title= Steelers Notebook: Pass-happy Hines Ward makes his 800th catch|url= http://www.post-gazette.com/pg/08364/938287-66.stm|series= Quick hits|work=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette|date= 29 December 2008|access-date=29 December 2008}}</ref>

Since his playing career ended, Gerela has worked as both a high school and college assistant football coach. In 2012, he became the head football coach of [[Gadsden High School (New Mexico)|Gadsden High School]] in [[Anthony, New Mexico]].

Gerela came from a particularly gifted family. His brothers were also professional kickers in the [[Canadian Football League]]; [[Ted Gerela]] with the [[BC Lions]] and [[Metro Gerela]] briefly with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] (Metro is enshrined in the ''Canadian Soccer Hall of Fame''.) In 1993, his son Ted Gerela was selected in the seventh round of the [[1993 CFL draft]] by the BC Lions as a linebacker from [[Rocky Mountain College]].

'''Ross Robert Verba''' (born October 31, 1973) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). A 6'4", 305-lb. [[guard (football)|guard]] from the [[University of Iowa]], Verba was a first-team All-Big Ten player in 1996.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/verba_ross00.html |title=Player Bio: Ross Verba :: Football |website=www.hawkeyesports.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110701104522/http://www.hawkeyesports.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/verba_ross00.html |archive-date=July 1, 2011}}</ref>  He was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the 1st round (30th overall) of the [[1997 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1997 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1997/draft.htm |access-date=March 30, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Verba was the first rookie to ever start a Super Bowl at [[offensive tackle|left tackle]], when the Packers faced the Denver Broncos in [[Super Bowl XXXII]]. He played four seasons for the Packers from 1997 to 2000, and three with the [[Cleveland Browns]] from 2001 to 2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ross Verba Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/V/VerbRo20.htm |access-date=October 5, 2022 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In June 2005, having failed to obtain an upgraded contract, Verba rebated his offseason bonus in order to obtain his release from the Browns.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/columns/story?columnist=pasquarelli_len&id=2081541|title = Verba released after repaying bonus to Browns|date = June 9, 2005}}</ref> After one season out of the league, Verba signed with the [[Detroit Lions]] for a final NFL season in 2006. He was released by the Lions on February 28, 2007, after spending eight games inactive with various injuries <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2783148|title=Lions release veteran offensive lineman Verba|date=February 28, 2007}}</ref> and being placed on injured reserve.

Verba was arrested on January 4, 2007, in Wisconsin on a felony warrant for writing bad checks in Nevada and released one day later. According to the [[Wisconsin State Patrol]], [[Nevada]] authorities lifted the warrant after Verba resolved a misunderstanding regarding an outstanding debt<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=2720317|title=Lions lineman Verba arrested on bad checks warrant|date=January 4, 2007}}</ref> of $50,000 at the [[Wynn Las Vegas]] casino.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.lasvegassun.com/news/2009/nov/26/judges-divorce-filing-follows-arrest-her-husband-l/|title = Judge's divorce filing follows arrest of her husband, a lawyer - Las Vegas Sun Newspaper|date = November 26, 2009}}</ref> Subsequently, Verba was arrested in 2009 on another Nevada warrant for failing to pay a $26,000 gambling debt at the [[Palms Casino Resort|Palms Resort and Casino]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.clevescene.com/cleveland/one-night-at-verbas/Content?oid=1489972|title=One Night at Verba's}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.las-vegas-criminal-defense-blog.com/2009/11/ross_verba_arrested_for_unpaid.html |title=Ross Verba Arrested for Unpaid Casino Markers to Palms Casino :: Las Vegas Criminal Defense Blog |access-date=November 16, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222014858/http://www.las-vegas-criminal-defense-blog.com/2009/11/ross_verba_arrested_for_unpaid.html |archive-date=February 22, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
